open_points.subject: owner_delivery flow
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: Does State 4 define an executable owner_delivery flow, an external behavioural sketch, or no flow at all?
options: An executable flow coordinates scan, placement, Portal publication and publication marking
An external caller must implement the described coordination
No owner_delivery flow is part of this product
open_points.default_guess: Define an executable orchestration flow while keeping Portal access outside the deliverer.

witness.initial: A confirmed project has one ready source photo and no placement or Portal publication.
events: The owner asks the calling flow to deliver the project's photos.
The calling flow can scan and place the photo.
outcomes: A kernel owner_delivery flow continues through Portal publication and marking, so the owner finds a hidden photo in the Portal.
State 4 supplies no executable flow, so processing stops after the primitive calls and no hidden Portal photo appears.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing the project's Portal photos

open_points.subject: owner_delivery invocation
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: Who starts owner_delivery, through what action or event, and which component executes it?
options: The owner explicitly invokes an agent-owned flow
A deterministic backend starts it automatically after a scan or schedule
Another workplace caller invokes the deliverer primitives directly
open_points.default_guess: An explicit owner action invokes an agent-owned calling flow.

witness.initial: A confirmed project contains a newly synchronized ready photo.
events: Syncthing finishes placing the file in the photo folder.
No further actor has yet acted.
outcomes: An automatic backend detects or schedules the work and delivers the photo.
Nothing happens until the owner or an agent explicitly invokes the flow.
witness.observer: The owner waiting for the photo to appear in the Portal

open_points.subject: scan step
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: Does owner_delivery call the deliverer's project scan operation, and which flow component supplies the project id and token?
options: The flow begins by calling scan for the selected project
The caller supplies observations obtained by a separate scan
The flow attempts placements from caller-supplied names and source ids without scanning
open_points.default_guess: Begin each run with an authenticated scan called by the flow executor.

witness.initial: A confirmed project's folder contains one ordinary ready photo whose name and source id are not otherwise known to the caller.
events: The owner starts delivery for the project.
outcomes: The flow scans the project, discovers the observation and can deliver it.
The flow requires caller-supplied observations, so this run has nothing to deliver.

open_points.subject: delivery selection, order and repetition
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: Which scan observations are delivered, in what order, and under what conditions is a placement attempted or repeated?
options: Attempt every READY observation in scan order and continue past per-photo failures
Attempt READY and PLACED observations until each is published
Deliver only an explicitly selected observation
Stop after the first attempted photo
open_points.default_guess: Process every READY observation in scan order, continuing past photo-local failures; use PLACED observations for publication recovery rather than placing them again.

witness.initial: A scan returns two READY photos in order; the first cannot be decoded and the second is valid.
events: The owner starts one delivery run.
The flow attempts work according to its unstated scheduling rule.
outcomes: The flow continues after the first photo's failure and places and publishes the second photo.
The flow stops at the first failure, leaving the second photo untouched.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing which photos arrived

open_points.subject: place-photo step
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: For each selected observation, which component calls the deliver-one-photo operation and how are name and source_id taken from the observation?
options: The flow executor calls delivery with the observation's exact name and source_id
A route delegates each observation to a separate placement caller
Placement is left entirely to an external caller
open_points.default_guess: The flow executor calls delivery with the exact name and source_id returned by the current scan.

witness.initial: A scan reports one READY observation and no placement exists.
events: The owner starts delivery.
The scan completes successfully.
outcomes: The flow calls deliver-one-photo and creates a placement.
The flow only reports the observation and creates no placement.

open_points.subject: Portal photo.publish step
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: Which component calls the Portal's photo.publish operation with M05 after a PLACED or REPLAYED delivery, and when is that call made?
options: The owner_delivery caller sends M05 immediately after a successful placement or replay lacking a mark
A separate publication worker sends M05 later
The flow returns M05 to the owner or another external caller and stops
open_points.default_guess: The calling flow, which holds Portal credentials, calls photo.publish immediately after placement or an unmarked replay.

witness.initial: A placement exists with its hidden publication body, but it has no photo_id mark.
events: The owner runs owner_delivery for the project.
The deliverer returns the placement.
outcomes: The flow calls Portal photo.publish, creating or retrieving the hidden Portal photo.
The flow stops with the publication body, so no Portal photo exists.
witness.observer: The owner reviewing hidden Portal photos

open_points.subject: record-publication step
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: After photo.publish succeeds, which component calls the deliverer's publication-recording operation with the returned photo_id?
options: The same calling flow records the publication immediately
A separate asynchronous reconciler records it later
The publication is never recorded by this flow
open_points.default_guess: The same calling flow immediately records the returned photo_id.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a mark and Portal photo.publish returns a photo_id.
events: The calling flow publishes the placement.
The run reaches the point after the Portal response.
outcomes: The flow records the photo_id, and the next scan reports PUBLISHED.
The flow does not record it, and the next scan reports PLACED.
witness.observer: The owner or operator viewing the next delivery run

open_points.subject: scan refusal
open_points.text: Refusal codes and failure members are those of States 1 and 2. The exact answers are decided in State 6.
open_points.question: What does the flow do when scan returns a refusal such as CONNECTION_NOT_CONFIRMED, FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE or STATE_UNAVAILABLE?
options: Stop the project run and expose the refusal to the initiating owner
Retry selected temporary refusals
Skip the scan and continue from previously known observations
open_points.default_guess: Stop the run and report the refusal; let a later invocation retry.

witness.initial: A project is confirmed, but its photo folder is temporarily unavailable.
events: The owner starts owner_delivery.
The scan returns FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE.
The folder becomes available shortly afterward.
outcomes: The flow stops and the owner sees a failed run requiring another invocation.
The flow retries and completes without another owner action.

open_points.subject: placement refusal or failure
open_points.text: Refusal codes and failure members are those of States 1 and 2. The exact answers are decided in State 6.
open_points.question: For each M08 refusal or FAILED PlacementOutcome, does the flow stop, continue with other photos, retry, or report a per-photo result?
options: Continue after photo-local M06 failures but stop on operation-level M08 refusals
Stop on every failure or refusal
Continue on every failure and refusal
Retry a defined subset before continuing
open_points.default_guess: Record and continue after photo-local M06 failures; stop the project run on M08 refusals.

witness.initial: A scan returns two READY photos; the first changes before delivery and the second remains valid.
events: The flow delivers the first photo and receives SOURCE_CHANGED.
The second observation remains available for processing.
outcomes: The flow treats SOURCE_CHANGED as photo-local, continues and publishes the second photo.
The flow aborts the project run, leaving the second photo unpublished.

open_points.subject: Portal publication failure
open_points.text: The exact answers are decided in State 6.
open_points.question: What does owner_delivery do when Portal photo.publish times out, refuses the body, or returns another failure after placement succeeded?
options: Stop without marking and retry idempotent publication in a later run
Retry publication within the same run according to a defined policy
Continue to other photos and report this photo as pending
Treat the placement as completed without Portal publication
open_points.default_guess: Leave the placement unmarked, report a publication failure, and safely retry photo.publish by intake_id on a later run.

witness.initial: A placement exists and has never been marked.
events: The flow sends photo.publish.
The Portal creates the hidden photo but the response is lost.
The owner starts the flow again.
outcomes: The flow retries with the same intake_id, receives the same photo and records its photo_id.
The flow assumes the earlier call failed or treats placement as complete, leaving either a duplicate publication attempt strategy or a permanently unmarked photo.
witness.observer: The owner and the operator inspecting scan status

open_points.subject: publication-mark refusal
open_points.text: Refusal codes and failure members are those of States 1 and 2. The exact answers are decided in State 6.
open_points.question: What does the flow do when recording publication returns STATE_UNAVAILABLE, NOT_PLACED, PUBLICATION_CONFLICT, or another refusal?
options: Report the refusal and retry or reconcile on a later run
Retry every refusal immediately
Treat a successful Portal publication as overall success despite the missing or conflicting mark
Compensate by hiding or deleting the Portal photo
open_points.default_guess: Report the refusal, make no Portal compensation, and reconcile through a later idempotent publish-and-mark attempt; surface PUBLICATION_CONFLICT for manual resolution.

witness.initial: A placement is unmarked, Portal publication succeeds with photo_id A, and another call records photo_id B first.
events: The flow attempts to record photo_id A.
The mark operation returns PUBLICATION_CONFLICT.
outcomes: The flow reports a conflict and leaves the existing mark B for reconciliation.
The flow treats Portal success as completion or retries blindly, concealing the disagreement between Portal photo A and mark B.
witness.observer: The owner or operator investigating the delivered photo

open_points.subject: recovery between Portal publication and marking
open_points.text: Written from the accepted States 0 to 3.
open_points.question: How does a later run resume when a placement exists and Portal publication may have succeeded but no publication mark was recorded?
options: Republish the stored M05 body using its stable intake_id, then record the returned photo_id
Only retry the mark using a photo_id persisted outside the deliverer
Leave the placement pending for manual repair
Treat every existing placement as completed
open_points.default_guess: Republish idempotently with the stable intake_id and then record the returned photo_id.

witness.initial: A placement exists, its Portal photo was created, and the process ended before recording the mark.
events: A later scan reports the source as PLACED.
The owner starts owner_delivery again.
outcomes: The flow republishes by the same intake_id, gets the existing photo_id, records it and reaches PUBLISHED.
The flow skips PLACED observations or lacks a recovery rule, so the placement remains unmarked indefinitely.
witness.observer: The owner and the operator viewing subsequent scan results

open_points.subject: flow completion result
open_points.text: The exact answers are decided in State 6.
open_points.question: What constitutes completion of owner_delivery and what result is reported when some photos publish while others fail or remain pending?
options: Return a per-photo aggregate distinguishing published, failed and pending work
Fail the entire run if any photo does not reach PUBLISHED
Report success when every attempted primitive call completed, even if publication remains pending
Return only the first failure
open_points.default_guess: Return an aggregate result and call the run fully successful only when every selected photo is published or has an explicitly reported terminal photo-local failure.

witness.initial: A run selects two photos; one reaches PUBLISHED and one fails decoding.
events: The flow processes both photos.
The flow reports its final outcome.
outcomes: The owner receives a partial result identifying the published and failed photos.
The owner receives a single success or failure and cannot tell which photo reached the Portal.

open_points.subject: owner review and show flow
open_points.text: The owner reviews a delivered photo and shows it to the client with the Portal's own operation.
open_points.question: What named Portal capability does the owner invoke to make a hidden delivered photo client-visible, and is review/show part of a State 4 flow or explicitly outside it?
options: A named Portal visibility operation is a later step of an owner review flow
The action is outside this service but its external capability and handoff are named
Publication itself may make the photo visible
open_points.default_guess: Keep delivery hidden, define review as a separate owner flow, and name the Portal visibility operation it calls.

witness.initial: A delivered photo exists in the Portal with client_visible false.
events: The owner reviews and approves the photo.
The owner invokes what an implementer interprets as the Portal's show action.
outcomes: A dedicated visibility operation changes the existing photo to client-visible and the client sees it.
An implementation treats publication or another unnamed action as the show step, leaving the photo hidden or creating a different publication.
